stem: Which clinical scenario represents an absolute indication for emergency fracture reduction before completing further investigations?

options.text: An obvious clinical deformity that threatens skin necrosis.
A fracture with severe pain that is well-localized to the bone.
An undisplaced fracture in a pediatric patient with an intact neurovascular status.
A fracture in a patient who has not yet received analgesia.

explanation: Pressure on the skin from an underlying deformity can lead to tissue death, necessitating immediate repositioning to relieve tension.
rationale: Consider which situation poses an immediate threat to the integrity of the soft tissue envelope.

optionExplanations.A: Pressure on the skin from an underlying deformity can lead to tissue death, necessitating immediate repositioning to relieve tension.
optionExplanations.B: While pain is significant, it is an expected symptom of most fractures and does not inherently require emergency reduction before investigation unless neurovascular status is affected.
optionExplanations.C: Undisplaced fractures with no vascular or nerve compromise can typically wait for formal imaging and elective management.
optionExplanations.D: Analgesia should be the first step in management, but the lack of it is not an indication for immediate reduction without investigation.

source.hint: Consider which situation poses an immediate threat to the integrity of the soft tissue envelope.
